name: tourbillon-cage
title: Tourbillon Cage
description: A full-bleed loading/route-transition curtain built as Breguet's tourbillon — a balance wheel ticking fast inside a carriage that itself turns slow, two rotations nested on one axis and never synchronized.
instruction: Build <TourbillonCage paused? children? className?> as a full-bleed canvas-2D loading/route-transition curtain modeled on Breguet's tourbillon (1795), the real watchmaking mechanism that mounts an entire escapement — balance wheel, hairspring, pallet fork, escape wheel — on a carriage that itself slowly rotates, so gravity's drag on the balance averages out over one carriage revolution instead of biasing it in a fixed orientation. COMPRESSED, NOT LITERAL, on both axes, stated as a departure not a fidelity claim: a real one-minute tourbillon carriage does one revolution per 60s, rendered here at CAGE_PERIOD_S=9s/rev; a real balance runs 21,600-28,800 vph (3-4Hz / 6-8 beats/sec), rendered at BALANCE_HZ=2.5 (5 beats/sec) — still well under the 60Hz paint rate so the tick reads as a distinct kick-and-reverse rather than aliasing into a strobe the way a literal 1:1 simulation would. ONE ROTATED CANVAS FRAME (ctx.translate to center, ctx.rotate(cageAngle)) holds the entire escapement subassembly — hairspring, balance rim+3 spokes, pallet fork, escape wheel — plus the carriage's own two asymmetric arms (a bare ns-muted counterpoise at 200deg, a foreground 'bridge' arm at 15deg carrying the escapement); rotating that ONE frame is what makes the carriage's slow turn legible, since the arm asymmetry is what actually sells the rotation frame to frame (a plain circle would look identical at every angle). The balance's own oscillation angle, balanceAngleRad(t) = BALANCE_AMPLITUDE_DEG(102deg) * sin(2*PI*BALANCE_HZ*t + BALANCE_PHASE), is applied as a SECOND, nested ctx.rotate() on top of the already-rotated carriage frame, composing the two rotations without either driving the other. THE PALLET FORK is the one high-frequency, high-contrast element: idx = floor(t / BALANCE_HALF_PERIOD) (BALANCE_HALF_PERIOD = 1/(2*BALANCE_HZ) = 0.2s) and frac = the remainder locate the current half-swing; a smoothstep eases 0->1 across the first 12% of that half-period (SNAP_FRAC) then holds, driving BOTH the fork's +-9deg rock (FORK_KICK_DEG, sign flips with idx%2) and the escape wheel's one-tooth advance (ESCAPE_TEETH=15, TOOTH_DEG=360/15) from the SAME clock, so fork and wheel release in lockstep the way the real parts are physically forced to — a genuine locking/impulse alternation, not a continuous spin: the wheel visibly steps one tooth and stops, steps and stops. The hairspring is a 6-turn Archimedean spiral (HAIRSPRING_TURNS) whose outer radius breathes +-6% (HAIRSPRING_BREATH) in phase with abs(sin(balance phase)) — stretching as the balance swings out. MONOCHROME: cage ring track (0.55 alpha) and escape-wheel rim/teeth and hairspring, all the quieter structural/supporting motion, stroke in --ns-muted; the bridge arm, balance rim+spokes and pallet fork, the fast climactic motion, stroke in --foreground, read via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) at mount and re-read on a MutationObserver watching its class, with NO hex fallback (readTokens runs synchronously before the first draw so nothing is ever read unassigned). --border is never used as a stroke. --ns-accent never appears anywhere — there is no pointer-driven highlight to reserve it for; the component takes no input at all. prefers-reduced-motion (and paused) freeze on STATIC_TIME = CAGE_PERIOD_S/8 = 1.125s (carriage at 45deg, a spread legible angle, never the unrotated t0 orientation), with BALANCE_PHASE chosen so the balance lands away from both a zero-crossing and a swing extreme at that instant, and the fork/escape wheel mid-hold between releases. Host follows the established canvas-2D full-bleed pattern (see curtain-leader-countdown): ResizeObserver resizes the DPR-capped (2) backing store, IntersectionObserver (threshold 0) and visibilitychange both stop the single rAF loop when offscreen/hidden, a 140ms poll picks up the paused prop without tearing down the effect. An aria-live=polite role=status sr-only div announces 'Loading' once for assistive tech; children render over the cage for an optional caption, scrimmed with bg-background/70 + backdrop-blur since the cage spans the full value range in both themes.
useWhen: Pick tourbillon-cage when a loading/route-transition moment should read as two independent mechanical rotations nested on one axis — a fast tick inside a slow turn — with no pointer input and no headline copy baked into the surface. Pick curtain-leader-countdown instead when the loading moment should read as a real countdown ticking toward a cut (numerals, a sweeping arm, a control-frame flash); pick weld-pool instead when the surface needs to carry a headline in the material itself rather than stay a content-free curtain.
